_why: Rows that update in place (issue #119) were refused renames on a real server night after night:
'Plex refused to rename ... (409 — a collection there already has that title)', while NO collection
anywhere held that title. Measured on a large production server (PMS 1.43.3.10793) on 2026-09-14 with throwaway
collections (a title marker like a row's, no shortlist_* label, deleted in a finally), and read from
Plex's own database, read-only.
1. A collection's title lives in the `tags` table (tag_type 2, `tag COLLATE NOCASE`). That table has
no library column: one name, one row, server-wide.
2. Deleting a collection leaves its tag row behind, with no taggings. Nothing Plex exposes removes it.
3. A rename (PUT /library/sections/{id}/all?type=18&id=..&title.value=..) renames the collection's
own tag row in place, and answers 409 when ANY OTHER tag row already has that name: an orphan
from case 2, or a live collection in another library. After a rename succeeds, the old name is free.
4. A create (POST /library/collections?title=..) is never refused on a name: it REUSES the tag row
with that name, orphan or live. Two same-named collections in different libraries (twins) therefore
share one tag row. Their memberships and deletions stay separate. Renaming ONE twin renames that tag
row and nothing else: the other twin keeps its title, the two stop agreeing with their tag, and
deleting a twin whose title no longer matches its tag left its items tagged (a stale name in the
items' Collections field). Plex does not refuse any of those renames.
5. So an orphaned name can be reclaimed without touching the row: create a helper with that name
(it takes over the orphan), rename the helper to a unique name, rename the row, delete the helper.
The row keeps its ratingKey and items. This must NOT be done when the name belongs to a live
collection in another library: the helper would share that collection's tag row, and renaming the
helper would move the tag away from that collection's title.
On a large production server at the time: 4 of 5 refused renames targeted an orphan left by the pre-#119 rebuild, 1 the
same person's live row in another library. 41 orphaned Shortlist tags in total.

cases.case: rename onto the name of a DELETED collection in the same library
same, plain title with no emoji or marker
CREATE with the name of a deleted collection
rename onto a name that was never used
rename onto the name another collection had BEFORE its own successful rename
rename a TV collection onto the name of a LIVE Movies collection
create a TV collection with the name of a live Movies collection
twins (same name, two libraries): each holds only its own library's items
twins: delete one, the other keeps its title and items, and can still be renamed
orphaned name: create helper with it, rename helper away, rename row onto it, delete helper
cases.result: row renamed, same ratingKey, same items

cases.case: twins: rename the Movies twin X->Y
cases.result: renamed; the TV twin's title stays X

cases.case: twins: then rename the TV twin X->Y (Y is the Movies twin's title)
twins: then rename the TV twin Y->Z, and the Movies twin Y->X
cases.result: both renamed; titles unaffected by each other

cases.case: twins renamed apart, then both deleted
cases.result: one item kept its tagging to the shared tag row

tags_table.schema: CREATE TABLE tags (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT NOT NULL, metadata_item_id integer, tag varchar(255) COLLATE NOCASE, tag_type integer, ...)
